tone_statements.citation: De Boeck, L. B. 1951. La tonologie des parlers du Nord-Ouest du Congo Belge. Bulletin des Séances, Institut Royal Colonial Belge 22: 900-919.
tone_statements.quote: Toutes les autres populations qui habitent, dans le District Congo-Ubangi, le triangle : Dongo sur l’Ubangi, Embouchure de la Mongala, Embouchure de la Ngiri, toutes ces populations possèdent le même type tonologique. ... 3. Mais tous les parlers possèdent la tonologie « Lingala déplacée ». ... la tonologie déplacée est une tonologie qui, en comparaison avec la tonologie normale, a déplacé le ton de chaque syllabe, de sorte que chaque syllabe présente le ton que possède la syllabe précédente dans les parlers à tonologie normale.
tone_statements.translation: All the other populations that live, in the Congo-Ubangi District, in the triangle Dongo on the Ubangi - mouth of the Mongala - mouth of the Ngiri, all these populations have the same tonological type. ... 3. But all the speech forms have the 'displaced Lingala' tonology. ... the displaced tonology is a tonology which, compared with the normal tonology, has shifted the tone of every syllable, so that each syllable shows the tone that the preceding syllable has in the speech forms with normal tonology.
tone_statements.summary: Areal survey: all 'swamp Bangala' speech forms, incl. Bomboma territory, have high/low tones, 'displaced' Lingala tonology (tones shifted one syllable rightward), word-to-word tone sandhi; no count.

tone_statements.citation: De Boeck, L. B. 1950. De tonologie der naamwoorden te Ebuku. Kongo-Overzee 16(5): 281-291 (with 'Slotbeschouwingen' on all six Ngiri varieties).
tone_statements.quote: Besluit : Na andere woorden veranderen de naamwoorden meestal hun toonmelodie en krijgen dan een, twee of zelfs drie tonen. De grammaticale klasse van het naamwoord brengt hierin een paar uitzonderingen. ... Samenvattine : De toonmelodie der naamwoorden ver- andert enkel na andere woorden. De algemene regel is hier een hoge begintoon erbij.
tone_statements.translation: Conclusion: After other words the nouns mostly change their tone melody and then get one, two or even three tones. The grammatical class of the noun brings a few exceptions to this. ... Summary: The tone melody of the nouns changes only after other words. The general rule here is an added high initial tone.
tone_statements.locator: section III 'De naamwoorden achter andere woorden', Besluit and Samenvatting, p. 285-286
tone_statements.summary: Noun tonology of Ebuku village speech: melodies in high/low terms, tone types A/B/C I-IV, sandhi after preceding words; no tone count stated.

sources.citation: De Boeck, L. B. 1949. Dialectgroepen in het Ngiri-gebied. Aequatoria 12: 87-94.
sources.note: Lexical isogloss bundles across the Bomboma, Nieuw-Antwerpen and Budzala territories; no prosody at all.

sources.citation: Grégoire, Claire. 2003. The Bantu languages of the forest. In D. Nurse & G. Philippson (eds), The Bantu Languages, ch. 19, pp. 349-370. London: Routledge. Section 2.3 Tonality, p. 357.
sources.note: Second-hand: Ngiri languages between the Ngiri and the Ubangi (Zamba, Lobala, Bomboma, Lingonda, Ebuku) 'have a very complicated tonality'; 'In Bomboma, nominal forms show tonal modifications that depend on their function and place in the clause.' Cites Toronzoni 1985 in its bibliography. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 1990. Parlers riverains de l'entre Ubangi-Zaïre: éléments de structure grammaticale. (Études Aequatoria 8.) Bamanya: Centre Aequatoria. Chapter 'Le parler des Ebuku', pp. 13-32.
sources.note: Nothing. Section 1 Phonologie (pp. 14-16) covers vowels, consonants, vowel harmony, coalescence, elision, gliding; 'Tonologie' (pp. 16-18) gives noun tone correspondences with Lingala-type tonology, high-toned prefixes in prepositional groups, final-syllable H in questions, tonal harmony from the final. No word 'accent'/'intensité'/'pénultième' anywhere in the chapter (the one 'quantité à la pénultième' remark at p. 69 is in the Libobi sketch, not Ebuku/Bomboma).

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 1989. Sur les parlers riverains de la Ngiri. Annales Aequatoria 10: 281-283; and Explorations linguistiques dans la Ngiri. Annales Aequatoria 10: 353-357.
sources.note: Classification and fieldwork diary (Ebuku = Lingonda notes collected at Mankanza, March 1988); Zamba singled out for a wholly different tonology (citing De Boeck 1951). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: De Boeck, L. B. 1950. De tonologie der naamwoorden te Ebuku. Kongo-Overzee 16(5): 281-291 (with 'Slotbeschouwingen' on all six Ngiri varieties).
sources.note: Noun tonology only (initial tone types, tone melodies before/after other words, high initial tone after another word, final tones lengthened before pause). Informant from Ebuku, 'sector and territory Bomboma'. No statement on stress/klemtoon. The only 'klemtoon' hit in the volume (16(1): 65) is Burssens's review of an Indonesian textbook, irrelevant.
